asymptotic expansions for timevarying scalar differential equations can be derived using the residue theorem of complex analysis for the discretized difference equations of the continuous-time scalar differential equations.

the asymptotic expansions for the solution of a time-varying differential equation are obtained by applying a fictitious time-dependent finite sampling period and by using the residue theorem to evaluate the solution of its discretized difference equation.

the asymptotic expansion formulas for the time-varying continuous-time scalar differential equation, with the time-dependent sampling period, are derived using the residue theorem of the discretized difference equation of the continuous-time scalar differential equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the asymptotic expansion for the solution of a differential equation using the asymptotic expansions of the solutions of their discretized difference equation with a fictitious time-dependent sampling period which tends to zero as time tends to the limit.
the asymptotic expansion formulas for the solution of a time-varying linear differential equation of the first order and of the Lyapunov equation.
asymptotic expansion formulas for solutions of time-varying differential equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymptotic expansion formulas presented in this paper are valid for all stable differential equations and all time-varying sampling periods, including the constant one.
the asymptotic expansion formulas presented herein are applicable to a large class of time-varying linear and nonlinear scalar differential equations.

the asymptotic expansion formulas for the solution of a differential equation are valid if the solution of the difference equation obtained from the discretization of the differential equation is stable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the asymptotic expansion formulas for the solutions of time-varying differential equations can be extended to the solutions of the discretized difference equations using the residue theorems.
the asymptotic expansions for the time-varying differential equations can be obtained by using a time-dependent sampling interval and a constant sampling interval.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the residue theorem for the asymptotic expansions of time-dependent solutions of differential equations requires a fictitious time-dependent finite sampling period which is defined as the ratio of each time instant to a positive integer which goes to infinity as time goes to infinity.
the use of the residue theorem for difference equations can provide a more general approach to the asymptotic expansion problem.
